stories.title: Mooresville Industrial Park Trades for $135M
stories.excerpt: A Blackstone affiliate sold the North Charlotte Commerce Center in Mooresville to CBRE Investment Management for $135 million. The Charlotte Business Journal reports the deal was part of a 2.3-million-square-foot portfolio sale that also included industrial parks in two other states. CBRE IM is an independently operated affiliate of CBRE Group. The North Charlotte Commerce Center is a three-building industrial park at 134 Serviceberry Way, 142 Serviceberry Way and 156 Exmore Road. It spans over 900,000 square feet. Strategic Real Estate Partners developed it on behalf of Blackstone’s Link Logistics. The building at 142 Serviceberry Way is the newest — and the largest — of the three, at 723,533 square feet. It was delivered in May 2024. The other buildings are 113,000 square feet and 90,000 square feet, and were delivered in 2022 and 2023 respectively. The post Mooresville Industrial Park Trades for $135M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Blackstone affiliate sold 900K-SF industrial park in Mooresville, NC to CBRE IM for $135M
Portfolio included three buildings; newest (723K SF) delivered May 2024, others 2022–2023

stories.summary: A Blackstone-backed industrial park in Mooresville, North Carolina—comprising 900,000 square feet across three buildings delivered between 2022 and 2024—traded to CBRE Investment Management for $135 million. The sale was part of a larger 2.3-million-square-foot portfolio transaction spanning multiple states. The deal signals institutional appetite for stabilized industrial assets in the Charlotte logistics corridor.
stories.impact: Limited direct relevance to multifamily development. However, the strength of Charlotte's industrial market and logistics demand (reflected in strong absorption and institutional buyer interest) often correlates with employment and population growth that supports residential demand in adjacent markets. Monitor whether this capital movement portends broader capital reallocation away from multifamily into industrial in the Charlotte region.

stories.title: Sandy Springs Okays Incentives for Mall Redevelopment
stories.excerpt: The City of Sandy Springs approved an incentive package to support Woodfield Development’s transformation of North River Shopping Center. The approval advances Woodfield’s planned redevelopment of the aging commercial center into a new mixed-use neighborhood featuring 336 multifamily residences, 85 for-sale townhomes, retail, restaurants and a new public park. Woodfield Development has approximately eight acres of the 13-acre North River Shopping Center site at 8830 Roswell Road under contract and will spearhead the redevelopment. To help advance the project and its community benefits, City Council approved targeted incentives.    The incentives include waiving the City’s recreation impact and permit fees, as well as a recommendation for the Sandy Springs Development Authority to authorize a 10-year property tax abatement. Together, the incentives are valued at just over $4.3 million and are contingent upon demolition of the existing shopping center and construction of the approved redevelopment and City park by Woodfield Development. Construction is expected to begin later this year. The post Sandy Springs Okays Incentives for Mall Redevelopment appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Sandy Springs approved $4.3M incentive package for Woodfield's North River Shopping Center redevelopment
Mixed-use conversion: 336 apartments, 85 for-sale townhomes, retail, restaurant, public park on 8 of 13 acres
Incentives include fee waivers and recommended 10-year property tax abatement contingent on completion
stories.summary: Sandy Springs, Georgia approved a $4.3 million incentive package—including fee waivers and a recommended 10-year property tax abatement—to support Woodfield Development's mixed-use transformation of the North River Shopping Center. The project will deliver 336 multifamily units and 85 for-sale townhomes alongside retail and a public park on an 8-acre portion of the 13-acre site. Incentives are contingent on demolition and completion of the development and city park.
stories.impact: Strong signal of municipal appetite to convert aging retail to residential-led mixed-use in Atlanta's northern suburbs. The tax abatement reduces long-term operating costs and improves development economics, making similar conversions in Sandy Springs and nearby Fulton County more feasible. Watch for similar trophy retail conversions in North Atlanta submarkets; tax-incentivized density near affluent, transit-adjacent areas is attractive for institutional multifamily capital and justifies higher land costs.

stories.title: Finmarc Acquires 460K-SF North Virginia Office Portfolio for $77M
stories.excerpt: Finmarc Management, Inc. has completed the $77.5 million acquisition of Highline at Greensboro, a two-building portfolio composed of approximately 460,000 square feet of commercial office space. The property consists of 8401 and 8405 Greensboro Drive, twin, 10-story office towers located in the Tysons Corner submarket of Northern Virginia, and were 70 percent leased and occupied at the time of the sales transaction. Cushman & Wakefield’s Paul Collins and Kevin Sidney represented the seller, CIM Group. Aaron Rosenfeld of Kelley Drye & Warren LLP provided legal services to Finmarc and Cliff Mendelson of Metropolis Capital Advisors assisted in the debt placement.The ten-story buildings totaling 460,000 square feet are comprised of 8401 Greensboro and 8405 Greensboro. The property is served by The Boro, a walkable amenity anchored by Whole Foods Market which includes 250,000 square feet of retail space featuring a diverse range of sit-down and fast-casual restaurants. The post Finmarc Acquires 460K-SF North Virginia Office Portfolio for $77M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Finmarc acquired 460K-SF office portfolio (Highline at Greensboro) in Tysons Corner for $77.5M

stories.summary: Finmarc Management purchased Highline at Greensboro, a 460,000-square-foot, two-building office portfolio in Tysons Corner, Northern Virginia, from CIM Group for $77.5 million. The twin 10-story towers were 70 percent leased and occupied at the time of sale. The transaction suggests investor conviction in stabilizing and repositioning office assets in the Tysons submarket.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development, but signals capital and developer energy concentrating in Tysons—a major job center and mixed-use hub. Office weakness and conversion activity in Northern Virginia (particularly in secondary office nodes) could unlock conversion-ready structures for adaptive reuse to multifamily, especially if Finmarc or peers pursue mixed-use repositioning. Monitor Tysons office fundamentals and zoning flexibility for residential conversion.

stories.title: Planet Fitness Takes 15K SF at Coney Island Residential Development
stories.excerpt: Wake up, it’s time for a workout. Planet Fitness has inked a 14,500-square-foot retail lease at the base of a new residential tower in Coney Island, Brooklyn, with Cammeby’s International Group and Rybak Development. Planet Fitness will move into the space at 532 Neptune Avenue next year on a 10-year lease with an asking rent of $65 per square foot, according to the New York Business Journal, which first reported the deal. Planet Fitness was represented by CBRE, while ownership was represented by Commercial Acquisitions. The names of the brokers on both sides of the deal were not immediately available. The brokerages did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s requests for comment. Planet Fitness has nearly 50 gyms in New York City across all five boroughs. The company did not immediately respond to CO’s request for comment. Cammeby’s and Rybak completed the three-tower, 499-unit residential complex at 532 Neptune late last year, featuring studio to three-bedroom homes. Some 30 percent of those units are designated as affordable housing. The development has 758,600 square feet of residential space, 40,368 square feet of ground-floor commercial space and 20,722 square feet of community facilities. The two developers aren’t stopping their work in Coney Island anytime soon, either, as Cammeby’s and Rybak submitted a rezoning application in March to build two 22-story residential buildings with a total of 703 units at 3030 Ocean Parkway and 400 Neptune Avenue. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Planet Fitness signed 14.5K-SF lease at 532 Neptune Avenue residential tower in Coney Island

stories.summary: Planet Fitness leased 14,500 square feet at the retail base of a newly completed 499-unit residential tower at 532 Neptune Avenue in Coney Island, Brooklyn, on a 10-year term at $65 per square foot. The three-tower residential complex was completed in late 2024 by Cammeby's International Group and Rybak Development. Planet Fitness brings nearly 50 NYC locations and strong tenant stability to the project.
stories.impact: Validates ground-floor retail economics and anchor-tenant demand in large Brooklyn residential developments. Strong retailer commitment (Planet Fitness, a national chain) at $65/SF in Coney Island signals sufficient residential density and foot traffic to support Class-B retail; this model works for contemporary multifamily+retail projects in outer-borough Brooklyn and Queens submarkets. Use as comparable for retail underwriting in similar neighborhoods with new residential supply.

stories.title: Related-Led Group Advancing 494-Boca Raton Apartment Community
stories.excerpt: Related Group, PEBB Enterprises and BH Group have begun work on Broken Sound Residences, a 494-home luxury residential community that marks the first milestone in the transformation of the former Office Depot corporate campus in Boca Raton. Once complete, the 28-acre destination will blend residences, retail, wellness offerings and modern office space into a single project. Designed by MSA Architects and construction led by Balfour Beatty, Broken Sound Residences will offer three distinct residential offerings. Broken Sound Residences will pair more than 23,000 square feet of indoor amenities with over half an acre of outdoor gathering spaces. Amenities include two pool decks, private cabanas, hot tubs, a cold plunge, a pavilion bar, outdoor grilling stations and lounge areas. Nearby, there is an additional pool, jacuzzi and resident wine lounge. Inside amenities include a hidden speakeasy lounge, private dining room, golf simulator, coworking lounges, resident clubrooms and a fitness center. An Equinox fitness campus will be one of the first tenants at the development. The post Related-Led Group Advancing 494-Boca Raton Apartment Community appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Related Group, PEBB, and BH Group started construction on Broken Sound Residences, 494 luxury units in Boca Raton

stories.summary: Related Group, PEBB Enterprises, and BH Group have begun construction on Broken Sound Residences, a 494-unit luxury apartment community on the former Office Depot corporate campus in Boca Raton, Florida. The 28-acre development is designed as a mixed-use destination incorporating residences, retail, wellness, and modern office space. Equinox will operate a fitness campus, and amenities include over 23,000 square feet of indoor space and extensive outdoor gathering areas.
stories.impact: Signals strong institutional capital and operational focus on corporate-campus-to-mixed-use conversions in South Florida. Boca Raton's affluent demographic and office-to-residential conversion thesis (leveraging existing infrastructure and land basis) creates a replicable model in similar markets where office cap rates have compressed and conversion rents justify redevelopment. Watch for similar Trophy-office-to-residential plays in West Palm Beach and Miami-Dade submarkets; this success could unlock institutional appetite for campus conversions across Florida.

stories.title: Get to Know the Broker: Jonathan Stein of Douglas Elliman
stories.excerpt: For Jonathan Stein, the best is yet to come. Stein, 43, joined the real estate game in 2015 after spending time in the private equity space and then going on the road with his best friend’s rock band, Phantogram, as the tour manager. Now, he runs the Jonathan Stein Team at Douglas Elliman. Stein oversees a group of eight brokers at the firm, which has worked on deals ranging from $1 million to over $45 million. When former New York Mets and current Philadelphia Phillies pitcher Zack Wheeler needed to sell his SoHo penthouse at 73 Wooster Street, Stein and team member Gavin Shiminski stepped in, helping the major leaguer sell the unit for $26 million. It was one of the five largest sales in New York City in July. The road to such a successful real estate career wasn’t easy, but Stein said real estate is an amalgamation of his favorite things: design, architecture, mixing different personalities, and working well with people. “I got into real estate the old fashioned way — my life blew up and I needed a new career,” he said. “I was waiting tables at a buddy’s restaurant looking for what was going to come next. A friend suggested real estate and I loved the idea.” Commercial Observer caught up with Stein in August for “Get to Know the Broker,” a series where we connect with residential brokers to learn more about what makes them tick. This conversation has been edited for length and clarity. Commercial Observer: What has been the biggest deal of your career? Jonathan Stein: I haven’t done it yet. Check back next year. We raised cattle and pigs, and I showed pigs in 4-H as a kid to help earn money for college. What’s your go-to takeout order? Sushi from my neighborhood omakase spot. stories.title: Rejection and Change Are Constants in Residential Brokerage. Adapt.
stories.excerpt: When I decided to get my real estate license, it’s safe to say I had no idea what I was in for. The perception of real estate agents is not the reality. A lot of people assume it’s about the money, but, for me, it’s really all about building and nurturing relationships. I’ve closed many deals by focusing on what was best for my clients, even when it required extra flexibility and problem-solving on my end. I realized early on that half the battle was just being available and accessible, and that building trust and transparency from the first call is key. As a young agent in the industry, I didn’t come into real estate with many connections. Most of my circle wasn’t ready to purchase a home or hire an agent for a rental. I had to find my own path, generating leads organically. But, as a young agent, I was extremely motivated to do so, and I was ready to adapt if needed. Mackenzie Kyle. PHOTO: Courtesy Platinum Properties One of my first deals was in the Financial District. My client’s mom found my profile on RentHop and called me out of the blue. We spoke about her search, and she asked if I could show an apartment in an hour. I lived an hour away from the building at this time, so I quickly rushed over. After a day of last-minute tours, I helped them find an apartment they loved. Their daughter was fresh out of school, and they were nervous about her moving to New York City, but, with my guidance and reassurance, they felt confident that the apartment was the right choice. I didn’t know this deal would jump-start my entire career, but it did. Not only do I still have an amazing relationship with these clients and have helped them find multiple homes, I was also connected with so many amazing referral clients from them because of the superior level of service that I provided. stories.title: Podcast: Using AI to Make Better CRE Acquisition & Underwriting Decisions
stories.excerpt: Steven Song is the founder and CEO of Diald, an AI-powered decision intelligence platform for commercial real estate. Before founding Diald, Steven worked on both the investing and development sides of real estate, and built his career across architecture and urban planning, training at Carnegie Mellon and the University of Pennsylvania. He was a founding principal at SCAAA, a global strategy, planning, and design firm, and is a partner at Axle Companies, a family office focused on real estate investment and social impact ventures. Steven is based in Los Angeles. stories.title: Machine Investment Group Closes Second Fund at Hard Cap of $350M
stories.excerpt: Machine Investment Group, LP, a New York City-based real estate investment platform focused on opportunistic, distressed and special situations across the U.S., reached the final close of Machine Real Estate Fund II, the firm’s second flagship investment vehicle. Fund II reached its $350 million hard cap in primary commitments and has raised an additional $120 million in co-investments to date. Fund II received support from a diverse group of new and returning institutional investors, including public and private pension funds, endowments, foundations, family offices and private investors. Fund II exceeded Machine’s debut fund, Machine Real Estate Fund I, which closed in 2022 with $246 million in primary commitments and $208 million in co-investments. “We are humbled by the support of our investment partners, including both returning Fund I investors and a number of new institutional relationships, which allowed us to reach our hard cap for Fund II,” said Eric Rosenthal, co-founder and managing partner of Machine Investment Group. “Reaching our hard cap in what continues to be a challenging fundraising environment, particularly for middle market managers pursuing a diversified strategy, is a milestone we do not take for granted.” Representative Fund II investments include a special situations powered land investment in Pennsylvania, a distressed 539-unit residential property in downtown San Jose, a 229-unit senior housing property on Long Island acquired out of a distressed situation, a recently developed 1.3 million square foot industrial park in Phoenix and a strategic capital investment in a publicly traded company being repositioned as a powered land and data center development platform. stories.summary: Machine Investment Group, LP, a New York-based platform specializing in opportunistic, distressed, and special-situation real estate, closed its second flagship fund at a hard cap of $350 million in primary commitments plus $120 million in co-investments. Fund II exceeded the 2022 close of Fund I ($246 million primary, $208 million co-invest) and drew support from institutional investors including pension funds, endowments, foundations, and family offices. The firm characterized the raise as successful despite a challenging fundraising environment for middle-market diversified strategies.
stories.impact: Signals sustained institutional capital appetite for opportunistic and distressed CRE despite rate volatility and multifamily headwinds. Machine's ability to raise a larger fund with a broader LP base suggests investor confidence in special-situations and value-add strategies across asset classes. For multifamily developers, this indicates capital availability for distressed acquisitions, preferred-equity solutions, and repositioning plays—especially in higher-barrier markets where operator expertise and capital cushion are competitive advantages. Monitor Machine's deal flow and sector allocation to gauge where institutional capital is targeting highest returns in a compressed-spread environment.
